distinguishing_features: Engineered heterogeneous nucleation sites on heat-exchanger walls, such as laser micro-channels or reentrant cavities, that fix where ice initiates.
Surface-mediated reduction of nucleation barrier and onset supercooling so ice starts at the wall rather than in the bulk liquid.
Flow/pressure control used to hold a small controlled supercooling that triggers nucleation at the engineered sites.
Wall-initiated frontal freezing intended to reduce stochastic ice bursts and solute trapping in juice ice.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce stochastic bulk ice nucleation and solute entrapment during juice freeze-concentration by controlling the initiation conditions of phase change at the heat-transfer boundary.
parsed.viable_reason: Textured heat-exchanger surfaces can plausibly provide heterogeneous ice nucleation sites, and the proposed bench comparison makes the claimed reduction in supercooling and nucleation scatter testable.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The closest art only retunes an operating setpoint to suppress spontaneous wall nucleation and provides no teaching or motivation to engineer surface nucleation sites to fix ice location and timing.
